items.title: Copilot code review billing will default to the organization
items.summary: GitHub says that from December 30, 2026, eligible Business and Enterprise organizations with no explicit Copilot code review billing selection will default to billing the organization that owns the repository. Existing explicit settings and important exceptions remain. This guide explains who pays, how to inspect the setting and how teams can estimate the impact without assuming a fixed review price.

items.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
items.summary: Google Research introduced Fuse in its November 25 article on verifiable social reasoning for LLM assistants. Its simulated scenarios separate what an observer knows from what a user actually tells an assistant, allowing researchers to evaluate how models handle incomplete social information. The approach aims to test reasoning under uncertainty rather than reward confident guesses about people.

items.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.summary: OpenAI's November 24 research announcement reports evidence of binding across five targets in laboratory work with Onava, alongside computational evaluations of protein-related capabilities in GPT-6-family research models. The results are an important scientific signal, but they do not establish reliable end-to-end protein design, clinical efficacy or replacement of specialized biology models.

items.title: Inside the Codex sandbox
items.summary: OpenAI detailed the Codex sandbox on November 18, 2026. Its default :workspace profile allows edits inside the project, keeps certain control directories read-only, permits broader reads within operating-system access and blocks network connections. SXF explains why those boundaries are useful but not a complete security guarantee, compares permission designs and supplies a concrete least-privilege review procedure for developers and administrators.

items.title: GitHub Copilot Evals is now in public preview
items.summary: GitHub introduced Copilot Evals in public preview on November 17, 2026. The tool creates and runs repeatable checks for Copilot skills, custom agents and MCP integrations, with human approval before each run and a local evaluation engine called Vally. SXF explains installation paths, a practical evaluation design and how to interpret failures and costs without mistaking demo results for evidence that an agent is safe or reliable in production.

items.title: Introducing ChatGPT for Sales
items.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT for Sales on November 17, 2026, combining a dedicated Sales plugin with more than 30 new or expanded partner plugins. Sellers can bring CRM history, account research and meeting notes into supported ChatGPT workflows, with access dependent on plan, region and workspace policy. SXF compares those workflows with a conventional CRM and explains how to verify data access, human approval and actual sales outcomes rather than relying on vendor anecdotes.

items.title: Strengthening NATO and allied cyber defenses with AI
items.summary: On November 17, 2026, OpenAI described its cyber defense work with NATO's Communications and Information Agency and allied public agencies, including authorized uses of Daybreak to investigate vulnerabilities, validate findings and prepare fixes. OpenAI reports NATO usage reaching up to 300 billion raw input and output tokens per month, and cites a Crossed Swords 2026 exercise organized by the NATO CCDCOE. SXF explains how to distinguish provider-reported operational activity, human-confirmed vulnerabilities and real security outcomes instead of assuming token volume is a defense effectiveness metric.

items.title: GitHub Copilot models deprecated on November 16, 2026
items.summary: GitHub deprecated Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra across most Copilot experiences on November 16, 2026. GitHub lists Claude Opus 5.5 for the first two and GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Luna for Terra, with specific exceptions for annual individual subscriptions and a runtime refusal fallback. SXF distinguishes removal from model pickers from legacy availability, and supplies a migration and permission-audit checklist for business and enterprise administrators.

items.title: VS Code retires the Local harness in February 2027
items.summary: GitHub announced on November 16, 2026 that VS Code 1.146 deprecates the Local harness for Copilot agent sessions, with removal planned for February 2027. The built-in Copilot harness has been the default for new sessions since version 1.143. Local computer use remains possible; changing harness does not automatically move files into the cloud or enable sandboxing. SXF maps session-runtime differences and provides a migration test plan for developer teams and managed organizations.

items.title: Broadening access to AI for scientists
items.summary: OpenAI announced November 16, 2026 that ChatGPT for Academic Researchers is expanding from a 20,000-person pilot to a program intended to reach up to 200,000 researchers. Applications for 50,000 new first-come, first-served grants open November 23, with eligible recipients able to include up to two collaborators and receive free ChatGPT Plus. SXF separates grant awards from seats and compares the Plus-based new round with the pilot's Pro access, while explaining why surveyed time savings are not a controlled causal measurement.

items.title: Hugging Face and OpenRouter join forces to make open-weight models easy to run
items.summary: Hugging Face announced on November 16, 2026 that its Inference Providers language-model traffic now goes through OpenRouter rather than Hugging Face's previous custom router. The company says existing integrations can continue using Hugging Face tokens and APIs, with provider routing based on price, speed and reliability, retries on failure and conversation-aware caching. SXF explains the important exception: customers can no longer pass custom provider API keys for these language-model requests, while image and video provider-key behavior remains different.

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot
items.summary: GitHub announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen availability in GitHub Copilot on November 13, 2026 across individual and organization plans, including Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise. The model is positioned for efficient agentic coding, tool use and multistep instructions, with gradual rollout and policy controls for enterprise administrators. SXF distinguishes Hydrogen from the already available Gemini 4 Carbon and the separate Google Search upgrade, and sets out a practical selection and evaluation procedure.

items.title: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
items.summary: On November 13, 2026, OpenAI announced ChatGPT Wallet with an initial rollout in dots for eligible US ChatGPT Pro adults using supported US-issued cards. Purchases require the user to review the cart and approve the payment with a security check. The launch did not set dates for Plus or international availability, and fully pre-authorized buying was presented as future work.

items.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem
items.summary: The ggml-org team announced version 1.0.0 of the llama.cpp and ggml libraries on November 13, 2026, clarifying semantic-versioning contracts for public C interfaces. Future API or ABI-breaking changes trigger major-version increments, while compatible features and bug fixes use minor and patch increments. The milestone matters to application integrators and package maintainers; it is not a claim that all backends have identical behaviour or that throughput improved by a measured percentage.

items.title: Manage AI Scan for repositories using the REST API
items.summary: GitHub announced on November 13, 2026 a public-preview REST setting called repository_scan to manage AI Scan for repositories at organization and repository level. The update allows settings automation via GET and PATCH APIs but does not automatically run a scan; users with repository write access start scans on demand, consuming GitHub Code Security AI credits. SXF explains inheritance, enterprise policy, conflict errors and rollout checks, differentiating configuration from scanning results.

items.title: Google Search gets a major upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.summary: Google announced the global integration of Gemini 4 Hydrogen into Search on November 12, 2026, aiming to interpret complex, multi-part queries and present more visual, structured results with links to relevant sources. A separate model launch establishes Hydrogen's developer positioning and published pricing. SXF separates the consumer Search experience from paid API access, examines what the launch can and cannot establish about traffic referrals, and offers a verifiable query-testing checklist for publishers.

items.title: Scaling AI value without losing control: Lessons from Frontier Firms
items.summary: Microsoft published findings from a commissioned IDC survey in November 2026 involving 5,204 IT and business leaders across 28 industries. The top maturity group reported average AI returns of 4x versus 2.7x among the bottom 30%, but these are leader-reported figures and do not establish that maturity caused the difference. SXF separates survey outcomes from causal claims and provides a practical framework for auditing measured AI value, agent controls and workforce readiness.

items.title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
items.summary: OpenAI announced on November 12, 2026 that it committed $2 million to a research network under the Coalition for Children's Rights and Protection in the Age of AI after signing a charter at the Paris Peace Forum. The announced goal is shared scientific measurement of AI's risks and opportunities for children, with researcher control over findings and publication of inconclusive or negative results. SXF explains what the commitment actually funds in principle and which independent checks are still necessary before claiming improved child safety.

items.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
items.summary: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API on November 11, 2026, powered by Gemini Decision 1, for probabilistic classification rather than general text generation. The announcement lists up to 1,000 questions per request, 256,000-token multimodal inputs and a $0.10 per million-input-token list price, with no output-token billing. SXF explains the difference between advertised model-compute speed and end-to-end latency and shows how to design human-review thresholds instead of treating a confidence score as proof.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon in GitHub Copilot
items.summary: GitHub's November 10, 2026 changelog announces general availability of Google's Gemini 4 Carbon model inside Copilot, with support across VS Code, Visual Studio, CLI, GitHub, coding agents and major IDE integrations. Access is listed for Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise tiers, under provider list pricing and usage-based billing, with a gradual rollout and admin model policies for organization plans. SXF explains the difference between availability and entitlement and adds an engineering review checklist for security-sensitive coding.

items.title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
items.summary: Google announced expanded Gemini Intelligence availability on November 10, 2026 for selected Pixel 10 models and Motorola signature 27, alongside Rambler speech cleanup, custom AI-generated widgets, device troubleshooting and expanded supported app task automation. Some features are planned over subsequent weeks and have restrictions on region, language, device generation, age and subscriptions.

items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
items.summary: On November 10, 2026, Google Cloud announced a U.S. preview of Gemini for healthcare, an enterprise system that combines specialized healthcare skills, clinical record connectors, controlled agents and audit trails. Read integrations for Epic and Oracle Health are listed among partner capabilities. The product is aimed at providers and payers, not at replacing clinical judgment or becoming a general consumer diagnosis service.

items.title: Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT
items.summary: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT beta on November 10, 2026. Eligible businesses can claim a profile in Business Hub, update their details and product feeds, and view aggregated data about mentions and website clicks. A separate Business Agent feature begins with eligible U.S. ecommerce and online-service organizations. Claiming a listing does not guarantee ranking in independent answers or access to a Business Agent.

items.title: Work at the Frontier: AI’s effect on freelance work
items.summary: OpenAI and Upwork published a November 10, 2026 analysis comparing ChatGPT activity with freelance marketplace postings. Of 63 matched work categories, 43 followed a pattern in which activities common in ChatGPT lost share on Upwork while less common ones gained share; 20 did not. AI-related job posts combined more varied tasks and often involved larger fixed budgets, but the study cannot prove AI caused demand changes or show what happens to all workers. SXF translates the findings into a clearer brief-design and skills audit.

items.title: Anthropic launches roadshow for proposed initial public offering
items.summary: Anthropic launched the roadshow for its proposed Class A stock IPO on November 10, 2026. The company describes 825 million shares offered, an expected $70–$78 price range, and an application to trade on Nasdaq under ANT. The U.S. registration statement had not become effective at the announcement. Neither a final offering price nor a confirmed first trading date was established in the release.

items.title: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together
items.summary: Amazon researchers published HOPE (Higher-Order Pruning of Experts) on November 9, 2026, a technique that selects experts to remove from mixture-of-experts language models while accounting for how pairs of experts cooperate. The team reports the best mean ranking among five pruning methods and an illustrative SWE-Bench Pro result of 42.3 after 50% pruning versus 41.8 for the original model. Those scores apply to specified models and tasks, not a guaranteed 50% reduction in total production costs.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic unveiled Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on November 9, 2026. The company says both use the same underlying model, while Fable applies stronger cybersecurity and biological safeguards for broad access and Mythos uses verification programs for specialized work. Anthropic advertises $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, with a higher-priced fast mode and company-run capability benchmarks.
